outcome: No event bearing on the monomial conjecture has been dated since 26 January 2024: the mixed-characteristic case was settled before the window (André's 2016 proof of the direct summand conjecture, published Publ. Math. IHÉS 2018, which André states directly implies the monomial conjecture, with Bhatt's 2016 quicker proof), and the equal-characteristic and dimension-three mixed-characteristic cases are older still; the only in-window items found are a 2024 Briançon–Skoda paper that does not address the monomial conjecture and two 2026 AI papers that resolve other commutative-algebra problems.
problem_asks: The frozen statement gives only the name 'Monomial conjecture on Noetherian local rings'. The formulation used here is the one in the Wikipedia article and the secondary literature (Hochster; Roberts; Dutta). Parts: (1) for every Noetherian local ring (A, m) of Krull dimension d, in every characteristic and residue characteristic; (2) for every system of parameters x_1, ..., x_d of A; (3) for every integer t (the article and Roberts write t ≥ 0, Dutta writes t > 0; equivalent, since t = 0 says 1 is not in the parameter ideal), the product (x_1···x_d)^t is not in the ideal (x_1^(t+1), ..., x_d^(t+1)). The equal-characteristic, dimension-≤3 mixed-characteristic and all-dimension mixed-characteristic cases are recorded below as context for the events, not as separate parts of the statement.

events.what_happened: Hochster (1983) showed that the direct summand conjecture (DSC) is equivalent to the monomial conjecture (MC). I know this only from quotations in secondary sources (Dospinescu's Bourbaki report, §1.6, which quotes '[Hochster 1983] a montré que la conjecture du facteur direct est équivalente à cette autre conjecture, la conjecture monomiale'; Hochster's lecture notes and Roberts' notes as summarised by search). I did not open the 1983 paper.
events.delivers: An equivalence between the MC for local rings and the DSC for finite extensions of regular rings. It resolves neither side. Per the secondary summaries, it is stated for local rings of residual characteristic p > 0 at fixed dimension, and in general.
events.remains: Everything. An equivalence transfers the question between two statements; it does not settle either.

checked_by.qualification: Research mathematician (CNRS) writing a Séminaire Bourbaki report on the André–Bhatt work
checked_by.what_they_did: Quotes Hochster's equivalence of DSC and MC in an expository report (§1.6); this is a citation, not an independent check of the equivalence

events.direction: Neither confirms nor refutes the conjecture; it links it to the DSC, which is the route later proofs use.

events.what_happened: Hochster and Huneke announced in the Bulletin of the AMS ('Tightly closed ideals', vol. 18 no. 1, January 1988, pp. 45–48) that tight closure gives simpler proofs of several results, including the monomial conjecture. The full treatment is 'Tight closure, invariant theory, and the Briançon–Skoda theorem', J. Amer. Math. Soc. 3 (1990), 31–116, DOI 10.1090/S0894-0347-1990-1017784-6. Both were found via search summaries; I did not open either paper. The AMS page returned HTTP 403.
events.revisions: Full treatment in J. Amer. Math. Soc. 3 (1990), 31–116.
events.delivers: The monomial conjecture for equal-characteristic local rings (rings containing a field). Tight closure is set up for rings of characteristic p and for algebras of finite type over a field; the search summaries say that reduction to characteristic p extends this to equal characteristic zero. Restricted to equal characteristic; says nothing about mixed characteristic.
events.remains: The mixed-characteristic case (p in the maximal ideal of a ring of characteristic zero), in every dimension. Dimension ≤3 there is covered by Heitmann; dimensions ≥4 by André (see the events below).

checked_by.who: Journal of the American Mathematical Society (refereed journal of record)
checked_by.qualification: Peer-reviewed journal; the authors are Hochster and Huneke, so this is publication, not independent review
checked_by.what_they_did: Published the full argument in 1990 (DOI from search results; article not opened)

events.direction: Confirms the conjecture for equal-characteristic local rings.

events.what_happened: Heitmann, 'The Direct Summand Conjecture in Dimension Three', arXiv math/0210223, submitted 15 October 2002. Journal citation Ann. of Math. (2) 156 (2002), 695–712, from Hochster's lecture slides (not opened). The paper proves the direct summand statement for mixed-characteristic rings of dimension three (the abstract does not say 'complete'). Via Hochster's equivalence this gives the MC in mixed characteristic and dimension three; that MC consequence is stated by Roberts and by Shimomoto rather than in Heitmann's abstract.
events.delivers: The direct summand statement for mixed-characteristic rings of dimension three, and so the MC there. Per the abstract, the direct summand statement was previously known for rings containing a field and for dimension at most two.
events.remains: The MC for mixed-characteristic local rings of every dimension ≥4, which was open until André's work.

checked_by.qualification: Commutative algebraist; author of the standard survey notes on the homological conjectures
checked_by.what_they_did: Wrote a published exposition of Heitmann's proof, 'Heitmann's proof of the direct summand conjecture in dimension 3', Math. Res. Lett. 10 (2003) 423–434 (per search summary; the paper itself was not opened)

events.direction: Confirms the direct summand statement, and so the MC, in mixed characteristic dimension three.

events.what_happened: Shimomoto, 'Almost Cohen-Macaulay algebras in mixed characteristic via Fontaine rings', arXiv 1005.3275 (May 2010). Gives conditional results: the MC for certain rings T between R and R⁺ under an extra hypothesis that the paper does not establish (Corollary 6.1), and states that 'the conjecture remains open for local rings in mixed characteristic of dimension at least 4'. Read via the ar5iv HTML.
events.delivers: Conditional and partial: the MC for some rings T between R and R⁺, under a hypothesis the paper does not verify. Recovers the dimension-three case from Heitmann's proof. No unconditional new case of the MC.
events.remains: The MC for mixed-characteristic local rings of dimension ≥4, and the MC in general, as the author's own 2010 status claim.
events.doubts: Conditional result, with the condition not established in the paper.
events.direction: Conditional support for the conjecture; no counterexample.
people: Shimomoto (given name not confirmed in my sources)

events.what_happened: Tavanfar, 'Reduction of some homological conjectures to excellent unique factorization domains', arXiv 1607.00025 (v1 30 June 2016; v2 28 July 2016). The abstract states that the Monomial Conjecture, the Big Cohen–Macaulay Algebra Conjecture and the Small Cohen–Macaulay Conjecture reduce to excellent unique factorization domains, and that 'some other reductions of the Monomial Conjecture are also proved'. Only the abstract was read.
events.delivers: Reductions of the MC to excellent unique factorization domains (and a few other reductions). Per the abstract, no ring class is settled outright.
events.remains: The MC for excellent unique factorization domains, and for every other class of local rings, as far as the abstract shows.
events.direction: Reduction only; neither confirms nor refutes.

events.what_happened: Dutta, 'Descent of Flatness and the Direct Summand Conjecture', arXiv 1611.04097, v1 posted 13 November 2016. It claims a proof of the DSC in all characteristics, without almost mathematics, from non-vanishing of Hom_R(B, R) for a complete regular local ring R and B the integral closure of R in the algebraic closure of its fraction field. v2 (17 November 2016) is withdrawn 'due to a gap in the proof of the main theorem'.
events.revisions: v2 17 Nov 2016, withdrawn for a gap in the main theorem.
events.delivers: As claimed in v1: the DSC in all characteristics, and so the MC. Nothing is established, because the paper was withdrawn.
events.remains: Everything, since the claim was withdrawn.
events.doubts: The author withdrew the paper, stating a gap in the proof of the main theorem.

withdrawn.what: v2 withdrawn by the author 'due to a gap in the proof of the main theorem'; v1 stands as the only public version of the claim

events.direction: Claimed confirmation of the conjecture via the DSC; withdrawn.

events.what_happened: Bhatt, 'On the direct summand conjecture and its derived variant', arXiv 1608.08882. v1 submitted 31 August 2016; v2 11 November 2017. The v1 abstract already describes André's proof as given ('André recently gave a beautiful proof of Hochster's direct summand conjecture'). Bhatt gives a shorter route, using a quantitative Riemann extension theorem for perfectoid spaces, that avoids the perfectoid Abhyankar lemma. Theorem 1.1: for a finite extension of Noetherian rings A0 → B0 with A0 regular, the inclusion splits as A0-modules. Also proves de Jong's derived variant (Theorem 1.2). Published Invent. Math. 212 (2) (2018) 297–317, online 15 November 2017 (Crossref metadata).
events.delivers: The direct summand statement for finite extensions of Noetherian regular base rings, in all characteristics and dimensions, by a second route. Bhatt does not state the MC; any MC consequence goes through Hochster's equivalence, which the text I read does not discuss.
events.remains: Nothing beyond André's theorem; Bhatt adds a second proof, not a new case.

checked_by.who: Inventiones Mathematicae (Springer; refereed journal of record)
checked_by.qualification: Peer-reviewed journal; the author is himself a leading expert in the area
checked_by.what_they_did: Accepted and published the paper, vol. 212 (2018) pp. 297–317, per Crossref metadata

events.direction: Confirms the direct summand statement, and so (via Hochster's equivalence) the MC in all characteristics and dimensions.

events.what_happened: André, 'La conjecture du facteur direct', arXiv 1609.00345, submitted 1 September 2016 (single arXiv version). Proves Hochster's direct summand conjecture using perfectoid theory (the perfectoid Abhyankar lemma and an analysis of Kummer extensions), after reducing to an unramified complete regular local ring of mixed characteristic. The main theorem, §0.2.1, reads (French, from the ar5iv rendering): 'La conjecture du facteur direct est vraie pour W(k)[[T1,…,Tn]] (donc aussi pour tout anneau régulier R)'. Théorème 0.7.1: for every complete Noetherian local domain B of mixed characteristic (0,p) there is a Cohen–Macaulay B-algebra C. The author writes, in the ar5iv rendering: 'Le th. 0.7.1 implique directement la conjecture monomiale', the monomial conjecture being equivalent to the DSC. Published Publ. Math. IHÉS 127 (2018) 71–93, DOI 10.1007/s10240-017-0097-9 (received 28 Aug 2016, accepted 20 Nov 2017, online 7 Dec 2017, per Numdam).
events.revisions: Single arXiv version (v1, 1 Sep 2016). Journal version Publ. Math. IHÉS 127 (2018).
events.delivers: The direct summand statement for all regular rings in mixed characteristic, in all dimensions (the author's own statement: W(k)[[T1,…,Tn]] and so every regular ring). By Hochster's equivalence, and by the author's own sentence that Théorème 0.7.1 directly implies the monomial conjecture, the MC for mixed-characteristic local rings in every dimension. The equal-characteristic and dimension-three cases were already established. The step from Théorème 0.7.1 and the DSC to the MC for arbitrary local rings of mixed characteristic is a reduction the paper relies on; I did not re-derive it.
events.remains: On the author's account, nothing of the mixed-characteristic MC is left open. The reduction from arbitrary mixed-characteristic local rings to complete domains and regular rings is cited, not checked, by me.

checked_by.qualification: Leading expert on perfectoid methods and big Cohen–Macaulay algebras
checked_by.what_they_did: Published a second, shorter proof of the same theorem in Invent. Math. (2018), so the theorem was re-derived independently by another expert; the paper also states that André 'recently gave a beautiful proof'

checked_by.qualification: Research mathematician (CNRS); author of a Séminaire Bourbaki report 'La conjecture du facteur direct (d'après Y. André et B. Bhatt)'
checked_by.what_they_did: Expository report on André's proof, stating 'elle a été démontrée par André en 2016' and quoting the equivalence of DSC and MC. This is an expert digest, not a line-by-line verification, and I read only the first ~100,000 characters

checked_by.what_they_did: Build on André's perfectoid method (abstract: 'inspired by the recent breakthroughs on the direct summand conjecture by André and Bhatt') to prove a related vanishing result; they do not address the MC
Unpublished note re-deriving the DSC from André's flatness lemma; see the separate event 'ma-undated-note'

events.doubts: (1) The sentence 'Le th. 0.7.1 implique directement la conjecture monomiale' comes from a fetched rendering of the French HTML that was summarised by a tool; the original sentence in the PMIHES text needs confirming. (2) Dating: Bhatt's v1 (31 Aug 2016) already describes André's proof as given, so an André argument was public, or at least circulating, before the arXiv posting of 1 Sep 2016. The first public written argument may therefore predate the recorded date by an unknown amount; the event is pre-window either way. (3) No erratum, criticism or gap report was found; the Springer/Numdam pages gave metadata only, and the full PMIHES text was not read. (4) The reduction of the MC to the DSC and to complete domains is cited from Hochster and not re-derived here.
events.direction: Confirms the conjecture (non-membership of the monomial in the power ideal) for mixed-characteristic local rings in all dimensions, through the DSC and the big Cohen–Macaulay route; no counterexample is involved.

events.what_happened: Heitmann and Ma, 'Big Cohen–Macaulay algebras and the vanishing conjecture for maps of Tor in mixed characteristic', arXiv 1703.08281 (v1 24 March 2017; v2 18 March 2018, labelled 'Final version'). Prove a version of weakly functorial big Cohen–Macaulay algebras in mixed characteristic sufficient for the Hochster–Huneke Tor-vanishing conjecture, and deduce a Boutot-type pseudo-rationality result for direct summands of regular rings. The abstract does not mention the monomial conjecture. Published Algebra & Number Theory 12 (7) (2018) 1659–1674 per search summary (not opened).
events.revisions: v2 2018-03-18 ('Final version'); published Algebra & Number Theory 12 (2018).
events.delivers: Weakly functorial big Cohen–Macaulay algebras in mixed characteristic, sufficient for the Tor-vanishing conjecture; not a statement about the MC.
events.remains: The MC is not stated as a result of this paper. A big Cohen–Macaulay algebra would give the MC by a standard argument, but the abstract does not say the paper draws that conclusion, and I did not check the full text for it.

checked_by.what_they_did: Published the paper in 2018 (per search summary)

events.direction: No direct bearing on the MC is stated; supports it indirectly through big Cohen–Macaulay algebras.

events.what_happened: Linquan Ma, 'A Short Proof of the Direct Summand Theorem via the Flatness Lemma', an unpublished note on Ma's Purdue web page (https://www.math.purdue.edu/~ma326/DSC.pdf). Ma's CV lists it as an unpublished note, and I found no arXiv posting. The date is not shown in the sources I could access; a search summary says it acknowledges discussions at MSRI in spring 2019, so it is no earlier than that. The PDF did not extract, so I did not read it; the claim below comes from a search summary: Theorem 0.1 says every complete local domain of mixed characteristic (0,p) with perfect residue field admits a big Cohen–Macaulay algebra, and so the direct summand theorem holds.
events.delivers: A shorter re-proof of the direct summand theorem, and so of the MC in mixed characteristic, relying on André's flatness lemma (per search summary). Not a new settlement.
events.remains: Nothing new, as far as the summary shows.
events.time_since_posted: unknown; no earlier than spring 2019 per a search summary
events.doubts: Read only through search summaries; the PDF was not extractable.
events.direction: Re-proof; confirms the direct summand statement, and so the MC, if the summary is right.

events.what_happened: Rodríguez-Villalobos and Schwede, 'The Briançon–Skoda Theorem via weak functoriality of big Cohen–Macaulay algebras', arXiv 2406.02433 (v1 4 June 2024; v2 4 September 2024, whose comment says 'to appear in the Michigan Mathematical Journal'; that acceptance is the authors' claim and I did not verify it). Proves a Briançon–Skoda-type property for the big Cohen–Macaulay closure operation, given a sufficiently functorial assignment of big Cohen–Macaulay algebras. The abstract says that, in mixed characteristic and using a result of Bhatt on absolute integral closures, this 'recovers a slight strengthening of a result of Heitmann'. The abstract does not mention the monomial conjecture.
events.revisions: v2 2024-09-04: minor changes and typos fixed; comment says 'to appear in the Michigan Mathematical Journal'.
events.delivers: A Briançon–Skoda-type containment for a big Cohen–Macaulay closure operation, under a functoriality hypothesis; in mixed characteristic, a slight strengthening of a Heitmann result. It does not address the MC.
events.remains: The whole monomial conjecture, which the paper does not address.
events.direction: Not applicable to the MC; the abstract makes no claim about it.

events.what_happened: Ju et al., 'Automated Conjecture Resolution with Formal Verification', arXiv 2604.03789 (v1 4 April 2026; v2 30 May 2026). Pairs an informal reasoning agent (Rethlas) with a Lean 4 formal-verification agent (Archon). The abstract says they resolved 'an open problem in commutative algebra' and formally verified the proof with essentially no human involvement. The abstract does not name the problem; the repository name 'Anderson-Conjecture' points to Anderson's conjecture (Cahen–Fontana–Frisch–Glaz Problem 8a). This is not the monomial conjecture, and I record it only as a neighbouring AI result.
events.delivers: Resolves an open problem in commutative algebra, which the repository identifies as Anderson's conjecture (weakly quasi-complete versus quasi-complete rings). Says nothing about the MC.

disputes.summary: Bhatt's v1 (31 Aug 2016) describes André's proof as already given ('André recently gave a beautiful proof of Hochster's direct summand conjecture'), but André's arXiv v1 is dated 1 Sep 2016. An André argument was therefore public, or at least circulating, before the recorded date, and the first public written argument may predate 1 Sep 2016 by an unknown amount. Both are pre-window, so the window count is unaffected.

summary: Searched 41 times on the web and read about 30 pages. The monomial conjecture was settled in three stages, all before the window. In equal characteristic, Hochster and Huneke's tight-closure work, announced in January 1988 and published in full in JAMS in 1990 (I read the announcement's abstract only through search, and the JAMS page returned 403). In mixed characteristic dimension three, Heitmann's preprint of 15 October 2002 proves the direct summand statement, and with Hochster's equivalence this gives the MC there. In mixed characteristic in all dimensions, André's preprint of 1 September 2016 proves the direct summand conjecture for regular rings; in the French text of his §0.7 he writes that Théorème 0.7.1 'implique directement la conjecture monomiale', and I read that sentence from a summariser's rendering of the ar5iv HTML, not from the PMIHES page. Bhatt's preprint (31 August 2016; Invent. Math. 212 (2018)) gives a second, shorter proof of the same theorem, and Dospinescu's 2023 Bourbaki report says it was 'démontrée par André en 2016'. Dutta's 2016 all-characteristic claim was withdrawn for a gap. Shimomoto (2010) and Tavanfar (2016) give conditional or reduction results only. Since 26 January 2024 I found no event bearing on the MC. Rodríguez-Villalobos and Schwede (June 2024) prove a Briançon–Skoda-type property and say nothing about the MC, and the two 2026 AI papers (Ju et al., arXiv 2604.03789; Jiang et al., arXiv 2605.25259) resolve other commutative-algebra problems; I checked the Rethlas list in its HTML and repository and the MC is not on it. The Wikipedia article (banner dated May 2024) gives only the characteristic-zero status and no mixed-characteristic status, and the list entry carries no status note. Close calls: (a) whether André's result settles all of the MC, since the reduction from the DSC and Théorème 0.7.1 to arbitrary local rings is Hochster's and is cited by André but I did not re-derive it; (b) what weight the single 'implique directement' sentence carries, since I could not read the PMIHES text. No AI system is involved in any MC event: the human-authored papers name none, and the AI-authored papers found concern other problems. The social-media lead (a pipeline using GPT 5.5 Pro and Claude Opus 4.8 on four commutative-algebra problems) could not be traced to a source naming the MC. A 2026 news item about the Jacobian conjecture (Fable 5) appeared in a search and is unrelated; I did not research it.
competing_reading: The strongest case against 'settled before the window' is that the mixed-characteristic result is one step removed. André's main theorem is the direct summand statement, and the monomial conjecture follows only through Hochster's equivalence and a reduction to complete domains; the 'directly implies' sentence is the author's own, but I could not read it in the published text. The Wikipedia article I fetched still states only the characteristic-zero status, which suggests the encyclopedia has not recorded a mixed-characteristic resolution. On a stricter reading, the problem counts as open in mixed characteristic dimension ≥4 until an independent check, and nothing dated since January 2024 changes that, so the window count would be zero either way.
what_would_settle_it: (1) The French sentence 'Le th. 0.7.1 implique directement la conjecture monomiale' and the surrounding text in Publ. Math. IHÉS 127 (2018) 71–93, read directly rather than through a summariser. (2) Hochster's 1983 paper, or a primary lecture note, stating the equivalence of the DSC and the MC for all local rings, with the reduction to complete regular local rings. (3) Any corrigendum, criticism or review of the André paper (zbMATH or MathSciNet review; the Springer page for DOI 10.1007/s10240-017-0097-9). (4) The text of Ma's unposted note, for its date and its claimed reduction. (5) The Wikipedia article's current status sentence and its talk page, to see whether it has been updated after André's result.

judgement.why: The monomial conjecture for all Noetherian local rings was settled before the snapshot: equal characteristic by Hochster–Huneke (case), mixed-characteristic dimension three by Heitmann (case), and all regular rings in mixed characteristic by André (2016, PMIHES 2018), with Bhatt's independent second proof (Invent. Math. 2018). Combined with Hochster's DSC⇔MC equivalence and André's own statement that his Théorème 0.7.1 directly implies the monomial conjecture, André's and Bhatt's events answer the whole statement; both were accepted by journals of record, so digested. Dutta's claim is withdrawn. Hochster's equivalence, Shimomoto, Tavanfar and Heitmann–Ma are reductions or adjacent results (none). The only post-snapshot items do not concern the MC: Rodríguez-Villalobos–Schwede addresses Briançon–Skoda (none), and the two Rethlas papers resolve different commutative-algebra problems (variant), so their AI credit, recorded for completeness, cannot attach to this problem. Ma's note is undated and gets null.
judgement.doubts: André's and Bhatt's main theorems are the direct summand conjecture; the step to the MC for arbitrary local rings rests on Hochster's 1983 equivalence, which the researcher read only through secondary sources, and on a summariser's rendering of André's 'implique directement' sentence. Bhatt's scope as whole relies on the same equivalence. Ju et al.'s AI role is coded from a thin quote that only names the agents; this has no effect, because the event is a variant.
